correctness.rationale: For any fixed odd positive h, local q² constraints on invertible p mod q² exclude exactly two units when q∤h and none when q|h. CRT plus PNT in fixed reduced progressions gives the finite-sieve product. For q≤X^(1/4), Brun–Titchmarsh bounds the summed large-square tail by O(X/log X∑_{q>Y}1/[q(q−1)]); for larger q elementary candidate counts O_h(X^(3/4)+X^(1/2))=o(π(X)). Hence Δ(h)=∏_{q≥3,q∤h}(1−2/[q(q−1)]). Direct local checks re-enumerated q=3,5,7 modulo 11025 for 9 odd shifts. The q=3 factor is 2/3; the elementary 3,5,7 lower product plus q≥11 tail proves C>1/2, so C≤Δ(h)<2/3 for 3∤h and 3C/2≤Δ(h)<1 when 3|h; endpoints sharp along odd primorial shifts. This is an infinite analytic sieve, not finite sample inference.
residual_risks: No claim of growing-h uniformity; finite check does not prove prime asymptotics.
